title: Satri-cel: first CAR-T approved for a solid tumour

research.what: CARsgen identified Claudin18.2 as a CAR-T target in solid tumours and took the CT041 product into early clinical trials. Origin: CARsgen's CT041 Claudin18.2-targeted CAR-T programme and early clinical trials from about 2018, followed by the CT041-ST-01 randomised phase 2 trial published in The Lancet

change.what: China's NMPA approved satri-cel on 22 June 2026 for Claudin18.2-positive advanced gastric or gastro-oesophageal junction cancer, the first CAR-T approval for a solid tumour anywhere.

note: It extends CAR-T cell therapy beyond blood cancers to a solid tumour, which had been the main barrier for the field.

security.note: No notable cyber implications beyond routine clinical and manufacturing data security.

title: Solid-state transformers for AI data centres and grids

research.what: Power-electronics transformers using fast semiconductor switching to convert medium-voltage AC straight to DC or low-voltage AC, studied in university labs such as NC State's for roughly two decades. Origin: University prototype work including the NC State (Lukic lab) solid-state transformer test and the long-running FREEDM-type research programmes (c. 2008 onward); year approximate.

change.what: Vendors plan customer pilots in 2027 and volume shipments from 2028; Heron Power's US factory is due to begin production in 2027 and reach 40 GW a year in 2029.

note: Could replace bulky iron-and-copper transformers, which face waits of up to five years, and cut conversion losses in data centres, solar and batteries.

title: BREST-OD-300 lead-cooled fast reactor with closed fuel cycle

research.what: A lead-cooled fast reactor with on-site mixed nitride uranium-plutonium fuel fabrication and reprocessing, developed by NIKIET under Rosatom's Proryv (Breakthrough) project. Origin: NIKIET BREST fast-reactor design (1990s) and Rosatom's 'Proryv' project (c. 2011); year approximate.

change.what: Rosatom has said physical start-up is planned for 2026-2027, with grid connection stated as the first half of 2027 in earlier statements and 2028 in a later one, at the Siberian Chemical Combine in Seversk.

note: It would be the first Generation IV reactor energy complex with a closed fuel cycle; the schedule has repeatedly moved and sanctions are cited as a difficulty.

research.what: Exploiting hydrogen that forms naturally underground and collects in reservoirs, rather than manufacturing it, following the first known commercial use in Mali. Origin: Bourakébougou well in Mali, the first known commercial use of naturally occurring hydrogen (drilled c. 2012, as described in the Oxford Institute for Energy Studies paper and the EFI Foundation report).

change.what: French developer FDE targets independent resource certification in 2027 and first commercial production in late 2028 in Lorraine, subject to permits; Mantle8 also aims to make natural hydrogen a reality by 2028.

note: Targets are company projections; commentators note that no engineered or natural subsurface hydrogen project has yet reached commercial production at scale.

research.what: Transporting pure hydrogen over long distances by dedicated steel pipeline, building on short industrial hydrogen pipelines in China. Origin: Sinopec's earlier short pure-hydrogen industrial pipelines (for example Jiyuan–Luoyang, 2015). This origin is from general knowledge and is not confirmed in the cited pages.

change.what: Sinopec's roughly 1,145 km Ulanqab to Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei pipeline demonstration is planned to be built and put into operation in December 2027, starting at 100,000 tonnes of hydrogen a year.

note: It would be China's first long-distance, cross-provincial pure-hydrogen pipeline, linking green hydrogen from Inner Mongolia to refineries in the east.

title: First phone NPU: Huawei Kirin 970 (Cambricon IP)

research.what: A Chinese Academy of Sciences team built a dedicated deep-learning processor architecture, which won a top architecture-conference best paper award. Origin: Cambricon / CAS Institute of Computing Technology deep-learning processor (2013 work, ASPLOS best paper)

change.what: Huawei launched the Kirin 970 phone chip with a dedicated neural processing unit built on Cambricon IP, and shipped it at scale in the Mate 10.

note: It put a dedicated neural accelerator into a mass-market phone SoC and started on-device AI as a standard phone chip block.

title: Intel Optane: first 3D XPoint storage-class memory

research.what: Intel and Micron began developing a stackable cross-point non-volatile memory built on chalcogenide phase-change/threshold-switch materials, positioned between DRAM and NAND. Origin: Intel–Micron 3D XPoint development from around 2012 (announced July 2015), building on earlier phase-change memory work

change.what: Intel shipped the first Optane products based on 3D XPoint in 2017, starting with data-centre and consumer SSDs and later memory modules.

note: It was the first volume storage-class memory with latency between NAND and DRAM, even though it was later discontinued.

security.note: Persistent memory keeps data in memory across power cycles, which changes the threat model for memory scraping and encryption.

title: Gate-all-around nanosheet transistors in volume (Samsung 3nm)

research.what: Gate-all-around transistors wrap the gate around all four sides of the channel; Samsung's version uses wide nanosheet channels (its MBCFET design). Origin: Samsung's proprietary MBCFET nanosheet GAA transistor development (start year approximate, not stated in the sources)

change.what: On 30 June 2022 Samsung started initial mass production of 3nm foundry chips using GAA, the first in the world to do so, replacing FinFET.

note: This was the first commercial move beyond FinFET transistor structure, and the industry has since followed with nanosheet GAA.

research.what: HBM memory with AI processing engines built into the DRAM so some computation happens inside the memory, which cuts data movement. Origin: Samsung HBM-PIM, announced February 2021 on HBM2 Aquabolt; later presented at ISSCC with AMD

change.what: Samsung put HBM-PIM into AMD Instinct MI100 accelerator cards and built a cluster of them, which Samsung and AMD reported cut energy use while raising performance in large AI/HPC tests.

note: This is the first in-DRAM AI compute demonstrated in accelerator systems. Sources describe the use as limited or prototype, so commercial volume is not shown.

title: WASI 1.0 and Component Model 1.0 stable standards

research.what: WASI defines a standard system interface for WebAssembly outside the browser. The Component Model adds language-neutral interfaces so modules written in different languages can be composed. Origin: The WASI system interface for WebAssembly, first published as 'preview1' in about 2019. It became WASI 0.2 with the Component Model in January 2024 and WASI 0.3 with native async in June 2026, under the Bytecode Alliance and the W3C WebAssembly WASI subgroup.

change.what: The WASI roadmap plans two-monthly 0.3.x releases through 2027, and WASI 1.0 may be scheduled outside that cycle. Other coverage expects 1.0 in late 2026 or early 2027. 1.0 depends on the Component Model reaching 1.0 first.

note: A 1.0 release would give a stable, portable server-side and edge runtime interface with compatibility guarantees. No firm 1.0 date has been published.

title: Korea's Independent AI Foundation Model programme (독자 AI 파운데이션 모델)

research.what: Korea's science ministry funds competing elite teams (Naver, Upstage, SK Telecom, NC AI, LG AI Research) to build foundation models designed and trained wholly in Korea, with GPUs, data and talent support. Origin: MSIT 'Independent AI Foundation Model' project, announced 20 June 2025 (formerly called World Best LLM)

change.what: The programme runs in six-month competitive evaluation rounds through 2027. It targets about 95% of the performance of leading global models, with open-source release to spread them into public and commercial services.

note: It is a state-backed route to nationally owned LLMs deployed in public and commercial services, with staged milestones through 2027.

title: FuriosaAI RNGD inference chip adopted for LG EXAONE

research.what: FuriosaAI designed its second-generation RNGD inference accelerator around its own Tensor Contraction Processor architecture, and LG AI Research began co-development and evaluation with it before the product was commercialised. Origin: FuriosaAI Tensor Contraction Processor architecture; LG AI Research collaboration and evaluation starting about two years before July 2025

change.what: In July 2025 LG AI Research confirmed adoption of RNGD for EXAONE after months of pilot testing, claiming 2.25x better performance per watt than GPUs, with enterprise EXAONE solutions planned on it.

note: A non-GPU Korean AI accelerator accepted for production large-language-model inference at a major conglomerate.

research.what: Tesla designed AI5, a 2nm-class inference chip rated at about 2,000–2,500 TOPS, to run its self-driving stack, the Optimus robot and data-centre inference. Origin: Tesla's in-house AI5 design, following its earlier AI4 self-driving computer, taped out in April 2026 with trial production at Samsung's Taylor fab

change.what: Tesla and its foundry partners (TSMC and Samsung) are targeting volume production of AI5 from mid-2027. Meaningful deployment in vehicles is expected later, and the schedule has slipped before.

note: This would be a vertically integrated automotive and robot AI chip made in volume at two foundries on a 2nm-class process.

title: SpinQ Gemini desktop NMR quantum computer (双子座)

research.what: Room-temperature nuclear-magnetic-resonance quantum computing in a spin-qubit lab at Shenzhen was turned into a small permanent-magnet two-qubit machine for teaching. Origin: Spin Quantum Computing Laboratory, founded Sept 2017 at SUSTech / Shenzhen Institute for Quantum Science and Engineering / Peng Cheng Laboratory (NMR and ODMR platforms)

change.what: Shenzhen SpinQ (量旋科技) launched Gemini in January 2020, billed as the first commercially available desktop quantum computer, and sold it to universities.

note: It put a real, maintenance-free quantum processor into classrooms at a price universities could afford, opening a quantum-education hardware market.

title: Quantum Origin: verifiable quantum randomness for keys

research.what: Randomness certified by Bell tests and processed with seeded extractors, so that key material is provably random. Origin: Device-independent randomness work from Cambridge (Colbeck's 2007 Cambridge thesis), later commercialised by Cambridge Quantum, now Quantinuum.

change.what: Cambridge Quantum launched Quantum Origin as a commercial cryptographic key platform seeded with verifiable randomness from a trapped-ion quantum computer. It later gained NIST SP 800-90B validation in 2025.

note: Described by its maker as the first commercial product built on a quantum computer to deliver a result that classical machines cannot match.

security.note: It strengthens cryptographic key generation against weak-entropy failures, and it supports post-quantum migration.

title: KAISER kernel isolation, basis of Linux KPTI against Meltdown

research.what: TU Graz researchers proposed KAISER, which unmaps most kernel memory while user code runs, to close side channels that defeat kernel address randomisation. Origin: Gruss, Lipp, Schwarz, Fellner, Maurice, Mangard, 'KASLR is Dead: Long Live KASLR', ESSoS 2017 (TU Graz)

change.what: KAISER became the basis of kernel page-table isolation, merged into Linux 4.15 and backported to stable kernels (the commit landed on 29 Dec 2017), with similar fixes in Windows and macOS, as the main Meltdown mitigation.

note: It was the first widely deployed software defence against Meltdown, reaching almost all PCs, servers and cloud hosts.

title: On-device AI detection of fake voices in calls (LG U+ ixi-O)

research.what: Anti-spoofing models that tell synthetic or altered voices from real ones, shrunk enough to run on a phone, so the call audio never leaves the device. Origin: LG Uplus in-house Anti-DeepVoice work with LG AI Research (voice activity detection, speech-to-text and anti-spoofing, trained on about 3,000 hours of call data), first shown at MWC in March 2025

change.what: LG Uplus released Anti-DeepVoice in its ixi-O AI call app on 30 June 2025. It flags forged voices within about 5 seconds, and the company says it is the first on-device commercial release of the technology.

note: It moves defence against AI voice-cloning phone fraud onto the handset, so no call data has to be uploaded to a server.

title: European Cybersecurity Alert System (cross-border cyber hubs)

research.what: A pilot funded by the European Commission linked national security operations centres (SOCs) across EU states, to share threat data and build joint detection tools. Origin: European Commission cross-border SOC pilot project launched in 2021; first phase of Digital Europe Programme consortia selected November 2022 (ATHENA, ENSOC)

change.what: The hubs are meant to become a working EU-wide network that pools threat data and issues real-time alerts. The European Court of Auditors says it is not yet functioning, and the ENSOC platform project runs to June 2028.

note: It would be Europe's first shared, near-real-time cyber threat detection layer across national SOCs. Delays in procurement, cooperation agreements and standards put the timing at risk.

title: NASA DSOC: laser communications across deep space

research.what: JPL developed a flight laser transceiver and ground laser terminals to test near-infrared optical links from beyond the Moon, building on earlier NASA optical-communication demos. Origin: NASA JPL Deep Space Optical Communications (DSOC) technology demonstration, described in a 2015 NASA/JPL project paper

change.what: On 14 November 2023 the DSOC transceiver aboard the Psyche spacecraft reached 'first light' and exchanged laser data from about 16 million km away, the first optical link in deep space.

note: First demonstration of laser (optical) communications across deep space, a route to much higher data rates than radio for future missions.

title: Queqiao lunar comms-navigation-sensing constellation

research.what: Queqiao relay satellites in Earth-Moon space, followed by the Queqiao-2 relay and the Tiandu-1 and Tiandu-2 test satellites, which were used to validate a lunar communication and navigation constellation design. Origin: Queqiao-1 lunar relay (2018) and Queqiao-2 with Tiandu-1/2 (2024), China's lunar exploration programme; the integrated constellation concept was presented in 2023 at the first Tiandu deep-space exploration conference.

change.what: China plans a pilot Queqiao constellation of lunar communication, navigation and remote-sensing satellites around 2030. It would support Chang'e-7/8 follow-on lunar missions and the International Lunar Research Station, with a fuller lunar backbone link by about 2040.

note: This would be China's lunar data-relay and positioning infrastructure. It is a published, staged national plan, not speculation.

title: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) for 6G coverage

research.what: Programmable metasurfaces that steer radio waves passively or semi-actively to extend and shape wireless coverage. They grew out of Chinese information-metamaterial research and theoretical RIS work from 2014 onward. Origin: Southeast University information-metamaterials team (Cui Tiejun) with China Mobile, whose 2021 Nanjing field trial of a tunable RIS followed the 2020 IMT-2030 (6G) Promotion Group RIS task force.

change.what: RIS is a listed key 6G technology within China's IMT-2030 programme, which is in its second trial stage (2026–2027). The first commercial 6G systems are expected around 2030, which is when RIS is expected to see real network use, with scaled deployment around 2035.

note: RIS is on China's 6G standardisation and trial roadmap. It is a coverage-enhancement component, not the whole of 6G.

change.what: Niron's Sartell, Minnesota Plant 1 is due to begin production in 2027 at up to 1,500 tonnes of magnets a year.

title: China 'AI+ Energy' plan: grid dispatch AI models by 2027-30

Origin: State Council 'AI+' action opinion (国发〔2025〕11号) and NDRC/NEA implementation opinion 国能发科技〔2025〕73号, 4 Sep 2025

change.what: By 2027 at least five sector-specific AI models are to be in deep use across grid, generation, coal and oil and gas, with ten or more replicable demonstration projects; by 2030 AI for intelligent grid control and new-energy forecasting is to be at scale.

note: It is a national programme with dated, countable targets for AI in power-system operation, so it is a published plan rather than speculation.

title: OpenGridFM: open foundation models for the power grid

research.what: IBM Research and Hydro-Québec started GridFM, an open framework for pre-training foundation models on solved power-flow and optimal-power-flow problems for grid analysis and operation. Origin: GridFM, originated by Hydro-Québec and IBM and contributed to Linux Foundation Energy; Joule perspective paper on grid foundation models (IBM Research)

change.what: A three-year US Genesis Mission Phase II project led by Brookhaven Lab aims to take grid foundation models from proof of concept to real-world use, simulating scenarios for adding new loads to the grid.

note: A funded multi-year programme with national-lab, utility and industry partners is moving a neural grid solver towards operational use.

title: Maximo: AI-vision robot fleet for solar module installation

research.what: AES developed Maximo, an AI-enabled robot that uses computer vision and generative image reconstruction to place and attach solar modules alongside crews. Origin: AES Corporation's in-house solar robotics programme (spun out as Maximo), unveiled in 2024 and developed with NVIDIA Isaac Sim simulation and AWS

change.what: AES deployed a fleet at the Bellefield solar and storage project in California. In March 2026 it announced 100 MW installed, which AES described as the move to sustained commercial production.

note: This is construction rather than O&M, but it is an AI-driven robot delivering clean-energy assets at utility scale. The research origin year is only loosely sourced.

title: Fully autonomous wind-blade inspection and repair robots (LEBO)

research.what: A Japanese startup built blade-crawling inspection and repair robots, paired with AI analysis of camera and drone images, to plan maintenance for each wind turbine. Origin: LEBO ROBOTICS Inc., a Japanese startup founded in 2018, which developed its own wind-turbine maintenance robots

change.what: Repair robots now run by a ground operator by remote control are expected to become fully autonomous within a few years of the August 2025 article, so around 2027-2028.

note: It would move wind-blade maintenance from remote-controlled robots to AI-planned work that runs without an operator.

title: AI-run O&M for remote renewable and grid stations

research.what: Combines large models, voiceprint detection, remote sensing, robots and smart wearables to monitor equipment and surroundings at stations in remote or harsh areas. Origin: NDRC/NEA 'AI+ Energy' Implementation Opinions (国能发科技〔2025〕73号), remote-station O&M task

change.what: China's plan sets AI-enabled intelligent O&M for stations in remote areas as an application scenario to be piloted under the 2027 and 2030 targets, supporting desert and offshore renewable bases.

note: The sources describe the scenario and the remote-base context, but no named deployment date or operator beyond the plan's 2027/2030 phases.

title: SECAI: edge-cloud AI heating control for housing stock

research.what: A German research consortium is building an AI heating controller that learns each flat's heat demand locally on an edge device and combines it with a cloud model and weather forecasts. Origin: SECAI (Sustainable heating through Edge-Cloud-based AI systems), a ZVEI research association project; first monitored heating season Oct 2024–Mar 2025

change.what: AI-based heating schedules and AI-recommended savings targets become a default service for landlords and tenants in existing buildings. The 2027 date is my estimate, not a date stated in the sources.

note: The project reports savings of up to 18% of heating energy. The sources describe a demonstrator and whitepaper, not a dated product launch.

title: SET Pilot 4: reinforcement-learning control of non-domestic building flexibility

research.what: Fraunhofer IEE developed an AI agent, using reinforcement learning, that runs an office building's heat pump and storage against dynamic electricity prices through the smart-meter infrastructure. Origin: SET Pilot 4 (Fraunhofer IEE Kassel with Smartplace and Teleseo), documented in a dena study published in 2026

change.what: AI energy management for non-domestic buildings that shifts load and sells flexibility, using the smart-meter gateway and a controllable edge component. The 2028 date is my estimate, not a date stated in the sources.

note: The pilot shifted load significantly. The sources frame wider use as future potential and give no dated rollout plan.

title: IA Eco-Pilot: AI control of public buildings (Grand Paris)

research.what: A French consortium (advizeo, Métropole du Grand Paris, Tilt) is developing AI that automates energy monitoring across about 7,000 public buildings. It is also developing predictive HVAC control, to be tested on about a dozen buildings in 6 local authorities. Origin: IA Eco-Pilot demonstrator, one of 8 winners of a French call for AI projects for the energy transition of territories, 2024

change.what: If the demonstrator succeeds, remote AI control of buildings combined with a flexibility offer is to be deployed more widely in the coming years. The 2028 date is my estimate, not a date stated in the sources.

note: The sources give only a vague 'coming years' timeline for scale-up.

title: AI Digital Convergence Platform for a fusion pilot plant

research.what: The Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory is building a fusion foundation model, a digital twin of the NSTX-U experiment and an AI computing infrastructure called STELLAR-AI to speed fusion pilot-plant development. Origin: Genesis Mission fusion work at PPPL (2025): NSTX-U digital twin, a fusion foundation model and STELLAR-AI

change.what: The DOE's Genesis Mission frameworks report ties AI-guided fusion engineering to a national milestone of an operational US fusion pilot plant on the grid between 2030 and 2035.

note: It treats whole-facility AI design and simulation as a way to shorten the fusion innovation cycle, which is separate from AI plasma control; 2030 is the start of the stated pilot-plant window.

title: Envision Galileo AI turbine with Tianji/Tianshu models

research.what: Envision built an energy-specific weather foundation model and a wind, solar, storage and power-market energy model, and fed live turbine data back into the weather model to improve forecasts. Origin: Envision Energy's in-house AI forecasting programme, which ranked first in China Southern Grid's power and load forecasting contests in 2022–2024.

change.what: In October 2025 Envision launched the Galileo AI wind turbine, which runs on its Tianji weather model and Tianshu energy model, after a demonstration wind farm had fitted the Tianshu control module to half its turbines since 2024.

note: It is a field-tested case of AI foundation models used for energy-asset design, control and forecasting. The company reports a revenue gain of about 20.9% against unmodified turbines at the same farm.

title: Power-industry cybersecurity large model (CEPRI, China)

research.what: A power-sector cybersecurity model was fine-tuned from the State Grid Guangming power large model on ten kinds of grid security corpora, and paired with the GridGraph power graph database to curb hallucination. change.what: In May 2025 CEPRI reported that the first power-industry cybersecurity large model was in live use; its intelligence-analysis, vulnerability-verification and attack/defence Q&A agents supported grid protection during the Asian Winter Games and the national 'Two Sessions'.

note: It is a reported first sector-specific LLM security assistant for the grid, with stated gains: intelligence analysis cut from 1-2 days to half an hour, and vulnerability-check accuracy up an average of 25%.

title: EU Network Code on Cybersecurity: first grid-wide cyber risk cycle

research.what: ENTSO-E, the EU DSO Entity and ACER drafted a sector-specific code for cyber-security risk assessment, minimum and advanced controls, and incident reporting for cross-border electricity flows. Origin: Network code on cybersecurity mandated by the Electricity Regulation (EU) 2019/943 and drafted by ENTSO-E/EU DSO Entity with ACER (2019–2022), adopted as Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1366

change.what: After the Union-wide report due December 2026, Member State-level risk assessments follow by mid-2029 and designated high- and critical-impact entities must then apply the controls, which in practice reaches real-world use in 2027–2031.

note: This is the EU's first sector-specific cyber rulebook for electricity, and it is the compliance baseline for any AI-enabled or automated grid operations. Sources do not describe AI-specific requirements.
